calls.headline: Gas cuts deepen to 33%, knocking fertilizer stocks and the EGX30
calls.body: The government raised gas curtailments for fertilizer and methanol plants to 33% from the 20% imposed on November 1, Mopco told the exchange, and notified Ezz Steel of a 30% cut with no end date (Asharq Business via EnterpriseAM). The reason is cost: Asian spot LNG rose about 36% in October to more than $34 per million Btu, a cargo now costs close to $120m, and five of the 15 cargoes contracted for November have been deferred. Abu Qir said two of its three plants still run at full capacity and it has rescheduled maintenance (Mubasher). Mopco fell 5.85% to EGP 38.60 and Abu Qir 5.78% to EGP 76.30 (Amwal Al Ghad), and the EGX30 lost 0.67% to 50,812.07. Fertilizer exports earned $2.53bn in the first nine months of the year.
calls.view: The state is choosing to save dollars on LNG at the cost of export earnings, and it gives no end date, so fourth-quarter volumes at Abu Qir and Mopco will fall. Both are already about 13–14% below their 50-day averages, and nine-month profits were large, so the fall is about the next quarters, not the business. Expect them to stay under pressure through November; a restored gas supply is the upside risk. For the pound the trade roughly cancels out: fewer LNG dollars spent, fewer urea dollars earned.
calls.wrong: The gas cuts are reversed before the end of November, or Abu Qir closes above EGP 85.

calls.headline: Egypt Aluminium's quarterly profit doubles to EGP 4.93bn
calls.line: The cheapest of the big industrials on earnings, with a state stake sale ahead.
calls.body: Net profit for July to September, the first quarter of its fiscal year, rose 104% to EGP 4.93bn from EGP 2.41bn, on sales up 6.35% to EGP 12.05bn (Arab Finance, Power News). Last fiscal year's profit was EGP 15.49bn. On the last 12 months that is about EGP 43.65 a share, or roughly 7.3 times Sunday's close of EGP 317.00, which is below its 50-day average of about EGP 338. Al Borsa reported last week that the state is studying a further stake sale on the EGX before year-end; no size or date has been given.
calls.view: Profit growing 16 times faster than sales means margins widened sharply, and at about 7 times earnings the stock does not price that in. A stake sale is the cap: new supply can hold it back for weeks, but the state wants a good price, which argues against a deep discount. The case is a move back toward the 50-day average by year-end.
calls.wrong: Egypt Aluminium closes below EGP 290 before the end of November.

calls.headline: Pound slips to 54.31 as bill yields ease at Sunday's auction
calls.line: A first slip after six gains, but the state still borrows a little more cheaply.
calls.body: The central bank's dollar selling rate rose to EGP 54.31 on Sunday from 54.01 on Thursday, a 0.6% slip for the pound after six straight gains; it is still about 3% stronger than at the start of November. At Sunday's auction the 91-day bill cleared at 24.86%, down from 25.00% a week earlier, and the 273-day bill at 26.26% from 26.36% (central bank). In stocks, foreign investors were net sellers of EGP 27.9m while Egyptians bought EGP 26.2m, on turnover of EGP 10.5bn (Amwal Al Ghad, Al Mal). Abroad, the dollar index closed Friday at 102.28, near its 52-week high, and markets price about an 81% chance of a December Fed hike (Reuters, CME FedWatch).
calls.view: One day's slip after six gains is noise; lower yields mean demand for local debt held. The desk keeps its view of a pound firmer than EGP 56. Tuesday brings two tests at once: US consumer prices, and Egypt's own October inflation, expected around the same day.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before the end of November, or this week's bill auctions clear well above 27%.

calls.headline: Results week: CIB on Wednesday, Telecom Egypt Thursday, Juhayna today
calls.line: The first company numbers since October's currency slide and the 100 basis point hike.
calls.body: Juhayna is expected to report today, CIB on Wednesday and Telecom Egypt on Thursday before the open. CIB's deputy chief executive, Amr El-Ganainy, said its Yomo digital bank has the central bank's preliminary approval and is completing the requirements for a final license (Banky). Telecom Egypt rose 0.9% to EGP 129.70 on Sunday, a fifth straight gain, after the Suez Canal Economic Zone hired it to upgrade networks across its ports and industrial zones (EnterpriseAM). CIB closed at EGP 127.31, just below its 50-day average of about EGP 129.2, up 23.6% this year; Telecom Egypt is up 97.2%.
calls.view: CIB's margins should show the benefit of higher rates, with loan growth the swing factor. Telecom Egypt has run up into its results and needs a clear beat; capex guidance matters as much as profit. Juhayna's report shows whether volumes held through price rises.
calls.wrong: CIB closes below EGP 118 or Telecom Egypt below EGP 115 in the two sessions after their results.

calls.headline: Houthis hit Riyadh's Aramco tower; Gulf markets fall, Suez traffic holds
calls.line: Houthi fire on Saudi Arabia is the main risk to the canal's recovery.
calls.body: Yemen's Houthis claimed a missile attack on Riyadh's financial district on Sunday that damaged Aramco's tower (France 24); Saudi Arabia's energy ministry called it an attempted attack with minor damage from falling shrapnel and no casualties. Saudi Arabia's index fell 0.8%, Abu Dhabi's 1.3% and Dubai's 0.3%. President Trump called new strikes on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress (Al Jazeera). Satellite tracking shows the canal still recovering: Suez transits averaged about 44 a day from October 1 to 18, up about 7% on October 2025, while Bab el-Mandeb fell to about 28 a day from 36 and Hormuz to about 4 a day from 89 a year earlier (IMF PortWatch).
calls.view: So far the Houthis aim at Saudi targets, not ships, and the canal keeps gaining; revenue of $724m in October shows bigger ships are coming back. If the fire turns to the Red Sea, shipping lines would leave again quickly, hitting Alexandria Containers and one of the pound's best new dollar sources.
calls.wrong: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping resume, or Alexandria Containers closes below EGP 29.

calls.headline: Nvidia's board opens an inquiry into Huang a week before results
calls.body: Nvidia's board said independent directors, advised by outside counsel, will investigate chief executive Jensen Huang after he admitted an affair with a woman whom The New York Times reported was seeking Nvidia technology for Chinese intelligence; her employer, Megaspeed, has bought about $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment (Al Jazeera). The board said it has no reason to think secrets were compromised and that Huang stays in charge. The shares slipped about 2.4% in overnight trading (Bloomberg). House Republicans want Huang to testify on November 18, the day after results. Asian chipmakers rose on Monday: TSMC jumped nearly 6% and Taiwan's index 5% (Euronews). Nvidia closed Friday at $186.64, 15% below its 50-day average.
calls.view: The story is now about governance as well as politics: an inquiry with no end date hangs over the results call and over Washington's appetite for Nvidia's China sales. It does not change demand, as Asia's rebound shows, but it caps the stock: expect it to stay below $210 into results, in line with the desk's open chip view.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $210 before its results on November 17.

calls.headline: Tuesday's CPI decides whether a December Fed hike is locked in
calls.line: Hike odds rose to 81% in a week; Fed officials keep talking up higher rates.
calls.body: October consumer prices are due Tuesday at 8:30am New York time, with an early FactSet forecast of 3.9% a year (CNBC), up from 3.7% in September (BLS). Markets price about an 81% chance of a December hike, up from 71% a week earlier, according to CME FedWatch (Reuters). On Friday San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the Fed will likely need to raise rates further despite the tech selloff, and New York's John Williams said inflation is too high (Reuters). The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.86% and the VIX at 25.64.
calls.view: A hike is the base case; the question is whether more follow. A print at or above 3.9% keeps yields high and weighs on the most expensive stocks, growth and 40-times-earnings defensives alike, while helping bank margins. A print below about 3.6% would spark a relief rally led by chips.
calls.wrong: CPI comes in under 3.6% and the 10-year yield falls below 4.60% by Friday.

calls.headline: Oracle loses a Tencent lease and Microsoft capacity in one week
calls.line: Oracle's AI backlog is shrinking from both ends.
calls.body: The FT reported that Oracle dropped a five-year, roughly $7bn deal to lease about 100,000 AI chips to Tencent from its Southeast Asian data centers after US officials raised concerns; Reuters said it could not immediately verify the report (DatacenterDynamics). Bloomberg reported on November 6 that Microsoft is winding down a 2023 deal to rent AI capacity from Oracle; Oracle said it has renewed or resold capacity at a 20% premium. Oracle hit a 52-week low of $111.60 on Thursday and closed Friday at $116.01, about 17 times the last 12 months' earnings (Nasdaq).
calls.view: At 17 times earnings much bad news is priced, but losing two large customers in a week makes the backlog, the whole case for its debt-funded build, less certain. Without a new anchor customer the stock lacks a floor before its December results.
calls.wrong: Oracle closes above $135 before its December results.

calls.headline: A SpaceX-Tesla merger would lift Musk's voting power to about 56%
calls.line: Merger talk can lift Tesla's price while worrying its other holders.
calls.body: Musk said on SpaceX's results call last month that both boards have formed special committees to study a possible merger. Barclays estimates that if SpaceX bought Tesla, Musk would own about 37% of the combined company but hold about 56% of the votes, since his SpaceX shares carry 10 votes each (Reuters). A change of control could also release market-value stock awards from his Tesla pay plan without its operating goals. Tesla rose 4.2% to $358.22 on Friday and is down 20.3% this year.
calls.view: Hopes of a premium support the stock in the short run, but holders would swap voting rights for a company Musk controls outright, and no terms exist. Without terms this is sentiment, not value.
calls.wrong: Tesla closes below $320 by the end of November.

The counterweights are a dollar near its 52-week high before Tuesday's US inflation data, lost fertilizer export earnings and the $10bn of foreign money Goldman estimates already left. Sunday's lower auction yields say demand held.

news.text: About 100,000 chips in Southeast Asia; Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

news.headline: Asian chipmakers rebound: TSMC up nearly 6%, Nikkei over 3%
news.text: Tech-heavy markets led Monday's bounce after last week's losses.

news.headline: SpaceX-Tesla merger would give Musk about 56% of votes, Barclays says
news.text: Both boards have formed committees to study a merger; no terms have been set.

global.finding: Brent traded near $96.35 on Monday, about 2% below Friday's $98.32, after Trump called new strikes on Iran "highly unlikely" if talks progress; gold rose about 0.7% to near $4,095, the dollar index eased to about 102.1 and Bitcoin fell to about $73,900.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel and LNG, so cheaper oil helps the import bill, but spot LNG has risen, which is why industry is being rationed; Brent near $96 is down from $98.32 on Friday.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram is EGP 7,115 on Monday, from 7,110 on Sunday, as gold in dollars edges back toward $4,100.
notes.dxy: At 102.28 on Friday, near its 52-week high, and about 102.1 on Monday; Tuesday's US inflation data decide whether it breaks higher and slows money into emerging markets, Egypt's included.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: about $73,900 on Monday, a fourth straight fall and down 15.5% this year.

news.headline: Trump calls new Iran strikes "highly unlikely" as a land blockade starts
news.text: Tehran warned it would "rain down hell" if attacks resume; talks cover its nuclear program and reopening Hormuz.

news.headline: Houthis claim a missile strike that damaged Riyadh's Aramco tower
news.text: Saudi Arabia called it an attempted attack with minor shrapnel damage; Gulf indexes fell up to 1.3%.

news.headline: Hormuz traffic near zero: about 4 ships a day against 89
news.text: IMF PortWatch counts for October 1–18 against a year earlier; Suez rose about 7% to 44 a day.

news.headline: Drone strike halts Iraq's Khor Mor gas field; Kurdistan loses power
news.text: More than 70% of the region lost electricity; no group claimed the attack.

news.headline: JPMorgan estimates a 1.4m-barrel-a-day oil surplus in October
news.text: Brent fell 16% last week, its steepest weekly drop since the pandemic.
